answer_1.quote: We focus on IC and VQA tasks, drawing samples from the MS-COCO 2014 validation set and the TextVQA test set. We compile generative outputs from mPLUG, LLaVA, and MiniGPT-4 to form the core dataset for MHaluBench.
answer_1.outputs: The outputs include image captions, answers to visual questions, and generated images from text prompts.

answer_2.quote: We compute the recall, precision, and Micro-F1 metrics individually for both hallucinatory and non-hallucinatory categories. Additionally, we assess the overall performance by measuring the average Macro-F1 scores at the claim and segment levels.

answer_3.quote: We instruct our chosen MLLM (GPT-4V or Gemini) to assess each claim's hallucinatory potential. In doing so, the MLLM also generates insightful explanations to elucidate the rationale behind its judgment.

answer_4.quote: We allocate the dataset uniformly across three annotators with graduate-level qualifications for independent categorization. Decisions in uncertain cases were initially held by individual annotators and later resolved by majority rule.
answer_4.guideline: Extracted claims are labeled as hallucinatory or nonhallucinatory, with a segment deemed hallucinatory if it contains any such claim; otherwise, it is labeled non-hallucinatory. An entire response is labeled hallucinatory if it includes even one hallucinatory segment.
criteria: whether the output text contradicts the information presented in the input image
whether the output text conflicts with world knowledge
whether the output image contradicts the information presented in the input text
whether the output image conflicts with the world knowledge underlying the text
